Secy. Home ... on 11 July, 2024

Author: Saurabh Lavania
Bench: Saurabh Lavania
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:47213
Court No. - 13
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 11790 of 2023
Applicant :- Ram Chander Tiwari And 3 Others
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Sectt. Lko And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Vindeshwri Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State of U.P. and gone through the record.

2. The present application has been filed for quashing the impugned summoning order dated 13.07.2023 passed by learned Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division) IIIrd/ACJM, Ayodhya in a Case No. 509/2006 (State Versus Ram Chander & others) in connection with Case Crime No.
509/2006 under section 498A, 504, 506 I.P.C & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act at Police Station- Kotwali Bikapur, District-Faizabad/Ayodhya and the proceeding of Case No. 509/2006.
Ram Chander Tiwari And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139918078/

entities.text: Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division) IIIrd/ACJM, Ayodhya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is stated that marriage of the opposite party no. 3/Smt. Sanju Mishra and the applicant no.3/Birendra Prasad was soleminized on 22.04.2000 according to the Hindu rites and rituals at Village Teekar, Police Station - Kurebhar, District - Sultanpur and on account of matrimonial discord on 06.07.2006, an F.I.R. was lodged under Sections 498-A, 504, 506 I.P.C & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act by the opposite party no. 2 namely Sri Surendra Kumar (uncles of opposite party no. 2) implicating the entire family of the applicant no. 3.
4.
After investigation, the charge-sheet was filed under Sections 498A, 504 506 I.P.C & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

The charge-sheet was challenged by means of Application No. 2597 of 2006 which was dismissed for want of prosecution on 06.09.2018 , a copy where of is Annexure No.
9.
5.

It is also stated that the applicant no. 1/Ram Chander Tiwari is father is law of opposite party no.
3 and the applicant no. 2/Rajendra Prasad and the applicant no. 4/Amit Prasad are brothers-in-law of opposite party no. 3.
6.

It is also stated that prior of lodging the FIR, the applicant no. 3 filed a suit under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act as suit no. 247 of 2006 (Birendra Prasad Vs. Smt Sanju) and thereafter a suit of no. 165 of 2007 seeking decree of divorce/dissolution of marriage was also filed by the applicant no.
3.
7.

entities.text: suit no. 247 of 2006 (Birendra Prasad Vs. Smt Sanju)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also stated that considering the aforesaid aspect of the case, the present application was entertained and interim protection was granted by this Court vide order dated 13.12.2023.

The order dated 13.12.2023, on reproduction, reads as under:
"1. Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicants is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. for the State.
2. The present application has been filed for quashing the impugned summoning order dated 13.07.2023 passed by learned Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division)
IIIrd/ACJM, Ayodhya in a Case No. 509/2006 (State Versus Ram Chander & others)
in connection with Case Crime No. 509/2006 under section 498A, 504, 506 I.P.C &
Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act at Police Station- Kotwali Bikapur,
District-Faizabad/Ayodhya and the proceeding of Case No. 509/2006.

3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that prosecution in question is a result of some matrimonial dispute and during the pendency of the case, parties came to the conclusion by way of settlement that all the criminal proceeding will be withdrawn by private respondents but the said agreement was not placed before learned trial court,
as a result, the summoning order was passed.
It is,thus, submitted that indulgence of this Court is required.

4. Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer of applicants but he does not dispute this fact that prosecution in question is a result of some matrimonial dispute.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A.
and going through the contents of application as well as other relevant documents; it is evident that prosecution in question is a result some matrimonial dispute, hence,
possibility of settlement of dispute cannot be ruled out.
In such circumstances, the matter requires consideration.

6. Issue notice to private respondents.
7.
List this case in the month of January, 2024.
8. Till the next date of listing, the impugned proceedings shall remain stayed in relation to applicants."

8. It is further stated that in terms of order of this Court, the service of notice upon opposite party nos. 2 and 3 is sufficient and despite the same, no one has put in appearance on behalf of private opposite parties.
9.

Further submission is that parties namely namely Smt. Sanju Mishra/opposite party no. 3 and Birendra Prasad/applicant no.3 have settled their dispute amicably and the suit no. 165/2007 has already been decreed on 31.10.2008 in terms of the settlement arrived between the husband and the wife i.e. the applicant no. 3 and the opposite party no. 3.

It is also stated that the application filed by the opposite party no. 3/Smt. Sanju Mishra under Section 125 Cr.P.C. has also been dismissed by the Court of competent jurisdiction namely Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 20, District - Sultanpur on 30.01.2010 and a perusal whereof would show that the trial Court dismissed the case after taking note of settlement between the parties.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 20, District - Sultanpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is also stated that the opposite party no. 3, after the judgment passed in the case no. 165/2007,
has started her new life and soleminzed the marriage.
In this regard, the reliance has been placed on para 26 of the application.

12. It is also stated that in view of facts and circumstance of the case particularly that in terms of compromise, the case instituted by the opposite party no. 3 under Section 125 Cr.P.C. has already been dismissed by the trial Court and the decree of divorce has already been passed and further that compromise itself indicates that the opposite party no. 3 does not want to proceed further in the matter including the pending criminal proceedings before the trial Court, the present application be allowed and the pending criminal proceedings be quashed.
13.

For the relief(s) sought, on the basis of compromise, the learned counsel for the applicants has placed reliance on the judgments of the Apex Court in the case of Romgopal and others Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2022 (1) SCJ 536, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab [2012 10 SCC 303], Mohd.
Ibrahim Vs. State of U.P., 2022 SCC Online ALL 106, Gold Quest International Ltd. Vs. State of Tamilnadu, 2014 (15) SCC 235, B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana, 2003 (4) SCC 675, Jitendra Raghuvanshi Vs. Babita Raghuvanshi, 2013(4) SCC 58, Madhavarao Jiwajirao Scindia Vs.
Sambhajirao Chandrojirao Angre, 1988 1 SCC 692, Nikhil Merchant Vs. C.B.I. and another, 2008(9)
SCC 677, Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others, 2008(16) SCC 1, State of M.P. Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, 2019(5) SCC 688, Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466, Manoj Kumar and others Vs. State of U.P and others (2008) 8 SCC 781, Union Carbide Corporation and others Vs. Union of India and others (1991) 4 SCC 584, Manohar Lal Sharma Vs.
Principal Secretary and others (2014) 2 SCC 532 and Supreme Court Bar Association Vs. Union of India (1998) 4 SCC 409.
14.

sentences.text: Learned Additional Government Advocate could not dispute the fact that the compromise has been entered into between the parties and now the opposite party no. 3 does not want to proceed with the proceedings in issue.

15. Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perusing the decree of divorce dated 31.10.2008 and order dated 30.01.2010 passed on an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. as also taking note of the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgments, referred above, and the nature of dispute/crime, this Court is of the view that no purpose would be served in keeping the proceedings pending before the trial court and hence, entire proceedings in issue are hereby quashed in terms of the compromise.
16. Accordingly, the present application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed in above terms.
